heading: What I work out by hand.
intro: Drawing is the part of my day with no protocol. Every piece starts on paper or canvas and ends when it stops asking me for something. Here's the story behind each one — and what it's made of.

shoreline.title: Shoreline at Dusk
shoreline.story: I painted the sky first and let it decide everything else. The daisies came last, almost as an afterthought, once the water needed something to hold onto at the edge of the frame.
materials: Palette knife for the horizon line

october.title: October
october.story: A studio afternoon that turned into a small ritual: one pumpkin, one moon, and just enough stars to make the dark feel intentional instead of empty.
materials: White paint pen for the stars

lily.title: Lily
lily.story: I kept building up the petals in thin layers until the pink finally looked like it was lit from inside instead of just colored in.

tulip.title: Tulip
tulip.story: The simplest subject I've drawn in a while, which is exactly why it took the longest: every petal only has one curve, and it has to be the right one.

mountain-lake.title: Mountain Lake
mountain-lake.story: Drawn from a photo I keep coming back to. I never get the mountains right on the first pass, so I've learned to draw the light on the water first and work backward from there.

cathedral.title: New Orleans Cathedral
cathedral.story: I was walking through New Orleans and a pen was the only thing I had on me. I didn't want to let the moment pass, so I drew fast, knowing I only had a few minutes before I had to keep walking. That's why the lines are loose — there's no correcting a pen.

lion-cub.title: Cub on the Rock
lion-cub.story: A warm-up sketch before a longer session. I drew this cub in a few minutes just to loosen my hand, and it ended up being the one I liked best that day.

seaside-brew.title: Moka View
seaside-brew.story: I'm only just starting to paint digitally, and wanted to begin with something small and familiar: the moka pot from every morning, set down in front of the sea. On paper I'd start with the drawing; here I started with color and let the shape show up on top of it.
materials: Soft oil brush for the sky and sea
Dry texture brush for the moka pot

window-view.title: Window
window-view.story: More of a practice exercise than a painting: I split the canvas into four and painted the same sky twice, day and dusk, just to get a feel for layers and blend brushes in Procreate.

full-moon.title: Full Moon
full-moon.story: I wanted to see how much I could say with almost no light. Most of the time went into painting the darkness in layers, not the moon itself — it turns out a night sky has more texture in it than it looks like at first glance.
materials: Soft light brush for the moon's glow

summer-umbrella.title: Summer Umbrella
summer-umbrella.story: A beach memory drawn in one sitting, no sketch first, just to practice letting my hand move as freely on the screen as it does on paper. The little dog half-buried in the sand was the last thing I added, and it ended up being my favorite part.
materials: Hard brush for the umbrella edges
